items.title: Smit Machchhar, PM Modi Invited To Light Israel Independence Day Torch As Netanyahu Hails Indian Pilot’s Courage

candidate_claims.text: World Smit Machchhar, PM Modi Invited To Light Israel Independence Day Torch As Netanyahu Hails Indian Pilot’s Courage Swarajya Staff Oct 04, 2026 | Updated 09:13 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere!

Sign In Prefer Prefer Israeli PM Netanyahu Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to light a ceremonial torch at Israel's Independence Day celebrations, calling the flydubai captain a "hero to Israel, India, and the entire world." The honour, traditionally reserved for Israeli citizens, recognises Machchhar's extraordinary courage in foiling a mid-air attack last week that could have killed all 174 passengers aboard.
During a telephone conversation on Saturday (3 October), Netanyahu told the 38-year-old pilot that he would be invited to light a torch alongside PM Modi at the prestigious Mount Herzl ceremony.
Netanyahu emphasised that the distinction represents Israel's highest honour, making the invitation to non-citizens highly unusual.
Machchhar prevented a catastrophic disaster on 30 September when his co-pilot attacked him with a crash axe during flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
